turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come in, sit down. What's the problem?

[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): It's the diarrhoea, doctor, and I was vomiting as well, it all started after my cousin Rachel's wedding on Saturday. I know I'm going on, but the meal was a buffet at the Regent Hotel in Cheltenham, and I had the prawns to start and then the chicken, which was a bit lukewarm if I'm honest.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): When did the diarrhoea start?

[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Sunday evening, around ten, maybe half past. I was absolutely fine on the Saturday, danced, got the last train. Well, actually Sunday after lunch I felt queasy, and by that night it had started properly. So we're on Wednesday now, that's three days, yes.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): How many times today?

[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): I did try to keep a tally. Um, four before I left the house, then one in the station toilet, and I think one more since, so five or six today. Yesterday I gave up counting after six or seven, might have been eight. Watery, yellow, nothing formed.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any blood?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I looked, because my mum always said look, and there's been no blood and no black stuff, just water really.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Vomiting?

[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Sunday night, twice, quite sudden, and then once more Monday morning before work. Nothing since about Monday lunchtime. The sick feeling is still there a bit, but I haven't actually been sick again.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Blood in the vomit?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): No, no blood. It was just the dinner, then a bit bile-ish the last time.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Keeping drinks down?

[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Since Monday afternoon, yes, little sips of water. I got those lemon rehydration sachets, Dioralyte, and I managed two of them yesterday. I did bring a mouthful of water back on Monday, but not since.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Passing urine?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Less than usual. This morning it was quite dark, just a small amount, which isn't like me first thing. No stinging or anything.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Dizzy?

[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): A little light-headed if I stand up too fast. This morning I sat on the edge of the bed for a minute. Not spinning, and I haven't fainted. I'm just washed out, tired in that floppy way.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Anyone else from the wedding ill?

[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, my sister Helen texted, she's got the same, and cousin Mark, and Mark's wife. All three had the prawns. My brother-in-law had the beef and he's fine, he even went to the gym yesterday, which is a bit showing off. So I do think it's the food.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Fever? Pain?

[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever that I've noticed. I haven't got a thermometer, so I can't swear to a number, but I don't feel hot or shivery. The pain is crampy, low down, comes in a wave just before I have to go, then eases. Not agony.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Been abroad?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): No, this was Cheltenham, not abroad. I nearly went to Spain in March and the flights got cancelled, but that's months ago and I was well, completely separate.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): Regular medicines?

[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Well, the water tablet every morning for my blood pressure, I've been on it for years. And I shouldn't have, but the chemist on Monday said don't take anything to stop it if it's food poisoning, and I took Imodium anyway, those little green and grey capsules. Two yesterday evening so I could get the train, and two again this morning. They barely touched it.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): Strength of the water tablet?

[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Two and a half milligrams, um, bendro-something, bendroflumethiazide, yes that's it, once a day. I took it at seven this morning with a sip of water, same as always. Last year at the surgery they did a kidney blood test and said it was borderline, no actual figure, just borderline. I was meant to repeat it and I don't think I ever went back.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): Allergies?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): None at all. Penicillin's fine, I had a course for a tooth abscess a couple of years ago, no rash or anything.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Mouth's dry. Pulse 98, blood pressure 112 over 74, temperature 36.7. Tummy's soft, tender low down, no guarding. Skin turgor is all right.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Is 98 worrying? I walked up from the car park and I always get anxious in waiting rooms, my heart races at the dentist as well.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): Mild dehydration, that's all. Stop the Imodium, it can drag a bug like this out.

[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Right, I won't take another. The box says one or two after each loose stool, and I'm sure it was just those four capsules in total. Do I carry on with the water tablet? I nearly skipped it, I'd read they don't mix with diarrhoea.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): Keep taking the bendroflumethiazide unless you stop keeping fluids down. Sip water or rehydration sachets through the day. No fizzy drinks and no dairy for now.

[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): Lemon Dioralyte then, I've a box of six at home. My sister swears blackcurrant is better, which I think is nonsense. I only managed half a piece of toast this morning, no appetite to speak of.
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): Either flavour is fine. If the diarrhoea is still like this in two days, or there's blood, or you can't keep fluids down, we'll send a stool sample. Not today.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): I brought an empty sample pot from the chemist, it's in my bag, I missed my chance this morning. So I just keep it?
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): If it hasn't eased in two days, come back, or sooner if you're dizzy, passing blood, or not keeping fluids down.

[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): So Friday-ish. Can I take paracetamol for the cramps? I've got the 500 milligram tablets, I took two last night and it settled a bit, but I wasn't sure alongside the Imodium.
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): Paracetamol is fine, two 500 mg tablets up to four times a day. Most likely a short-lived food-related gastroenteritis. Nothing else on examination beyond that dryness.

[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Helen's worse than me and she won't come in, she's stubborn. Should I tell her the same, and do I ring the hotel? There were about sixty of us and I still feel I should have said the chicken was lukewarm.
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): Tell her fluids, no loperamide, and to be seen if she worsens. The hotel's your call. You know when to come back.

omissions.text: Diarrhoea described as watery/yellow with nothing formed.
Patient had one mouthful of water come back up on Monday but has been keeping drinks down since Monday afternoon.
No spinning vertigo was reported with the dizziness/light-headedness.
Abdominal pain was described as crampy low down, coming in waves just before needing to open bowels, then easing, and not severe ('not agony').
No shivers/feeling hot reported with the questioned fever history ('don't feel hot or shivery').
Possible food exposure details were given: buffet at the Regent Hotel in Cheltenham, ate prawns and lukewarm chicken.
Several other wedding attendees were unwell: sister Helen, cousin Mark, and Mark's wife; all three had the prawns, whereas brother-in-law who had beef was well.
Patient took bendroflumethiazide at 7 this morning with a sip of water.
Kidney blood test history included that the result was said to be 'borderline' and the patient was supposed to repeat it but did not return.
Paracetamol entry is wrong: the patient reported taking two 500 mg tablets last night, not a single 500 mg dose.
